levels.name: First Steps
levels.briefing: Learn to gather, build and train. The Alliance is slow to react.
hints: Click a peon to select it, then right-click a gold mine or a tree: it gathers and brings the load to the Great Hall.
Gold and lumber are at the top of the screen. The last number is food: every unit eats, so build Pig Farms.
With a peon selected, press Build and pick a Pig Farm, then click where it should go.
A Barracks trains Grunts. Select it, click a Grunt, and set a rally point with a right-click.
Drag a box to select an army, then right-click an enemy to attack. Destroy every Alliance unit and building to win.

levels.name: Ranged Fighters
levels.briefing: Axethrowers hit from afar; keep tougher units in front.
hints: Troll Axethrowers attack from a distance but are fragile: let Grunts take the blows.
Use the Attack button and click the ground to attack-move: the army fights whatever it meets on the way.
Ranged units fire visible missiles. Keep them back, behind your front line.

levels.name: Heavy Hitters
hints: The Ogre Mound trains Ogres (strong in melee) and Catapults.
Catapults outrange everything and are deadly to buildings, but are slow and weak up close: escort them.
Mix the army: Ogres in front, Axethrowers and Catapults behind.

levels.name: Dark Arts
levels.briefing: The Temple of the Damned opens up.
hints: Death Knights are the strongest ground units. Their Temple is costly, so expand your gold first.
Watch the minimap (top left): red dots are the Alliance. Click it to jump the camera there.

levels.name: Full Army
levels.briefing: Everything on foot, against larger waves.
hints: The Alliance now attacks in bigger waves. Keep an army near your Great Hall.
Winning is about economy as much as fighting: more peons on gold means a bigger army sooner.

levels.name: Wings Over the Cliffs
levels.briefing: The Alliance cannot be reached on foot. Take to the sky.
hints: No land route connects the two bases. Fly: select a peon, Build a Dragon Roost, and train Dragons.
Dragons fly over any terrain and breathe fire, but they cost food and gold. Zeppelins (Alchemist) are cheap scouts.
Alliance Gryphons will come for you. Dragons are good at fighting them: keep a few at home.

levels.name: Frozen Skies
levels.briefing: A winter map and a bigger Alliance air force.
hints: Your ground army cannot cross, so spend on Dragons and farms to feed them.

levels.name: Islands in the Mist
hints: Scout with a Zeppelin: its sight range is long and it is cheap.

levels.name: The Last Mines
levels.briefing: Gold everywhere, walled in by rock: only the air gets through.
hints: Defend the Great Hall while your dragons strike; the Alliance Gryphons target whatever is exposed.

levels.name: Out to Sea
levels.briefing: The first fleet. Learn the shipyard and the tankers.
hints: A Shipyard (Build menu) must stand on the shore. It trains Oil Tankers, Destroyers and the big warships.
Ships cost oil. Train Oil Tankers, select them and right-click an oil patch (the black pools at sea): they pump it and deliver to the Shipyard.
Destroyers fight at range; the big ships (Juggernaut or Battleship) bombard coasts, but cannot go on land: use them with dragons to finish what stands inland.

levels.name: Ice and Iron
levels.briefing: Narrow waters: the enemy fleet will come through the fjords.
hints: Keep your warships together: a lone destroyer loses to a pack.
Your tankers are defenceless. Keep them close to the Shipyard and away from enemy ships.

levels.name: Island War
levels.briefing: A map of islands and oil. Whoever controls the sea wins.
hints: Send your fleet to the enemy coast with an attack-move (Attack, then click the sea near their base).

levels.name: The Long Voyage
levels.briefing: A very long way around by sea.

levels.name: Rich Ground
levels.briefing: Everything is available; the Alliance is not idle.
hints: All units and buildings are yours. Combine ground and air.

levels.name: Mountain Pass
levels.briefing: The final push through the mountains.
